text:
Jordan: quick sync: i'm trying to reconcile how paging should look across python/ts/go. two axes: iterator ergonomics and where retries/live resume live. thoughts?
Priya: i'd keep language idiomatic but consistent names: ListFoos, ListFoosPager, ListFoosStream. Pager returns pages, iterator yields items.
Noah: agree on names. major decision: make resume token opaque (clients treat as string) or expose structured cursor? opaque wins for forward-compat.
Rae: opaque token + stable version header seems fine. need a token migration story (v1->v2). SDK should parse a small prefix like "v1:" to detect version.
Jordan: regarding retries: low-level idempotent retries should live in transport. higher-level page retries (when next_token fetch fails) should be retried by Pager with backoff but only for transient errors.
Priya: explicit opt-in for automatic page-retry? some callers want strict single-request semantics. maybe Pager has retry_policy optional param. default: enabled for transient network errors.
Noah: transport interface idea: {unary, stream, resume} where resume takes a token and returns a page. languages map paging to resume when token exists, otherwise call unary+iterate. stream->pager adapter can buffer server page markers.
Rae: notable edge: streaming endpoints (grpc server-stream) may not emit page tokens. stream->pager adapter must not buffer unboundedly; add a max_page_size guard and stream timeout. Document tradeoffs.
Jordan: go ergonomics: prefer explicit Pager.Next(ctx) bool + Pager.Items() []Item. avoid Go channels for this surface to keep deterministic cancellation and error handling.
Priya: python: provide async iterator and a sync wrapper that runs it in an event loop for convenience. ts: async iterator + a .byPage() helper like existing JS pattern.
Noah: about non-idempotent backends: we need an API metadata flag stable_for_pagination that servers can declare. SDK should warn if using auto-dedupe or aggressive retries against unstable endpoints.
Rae: tests: roundtrip token tests, cross-lang resume parity, stream->pager correctness (ordering + duplicates), and perf for buffering. add integration tests with small dataset to simulate concurrent writes between pages.
Jordan: rollout plan: 1) PR spec for token format + migration, 2) add TransportAdapter interface to all SDK repos, 3) implement Pager types in python/ts, 4) cross-lang parity tests, 5) opt-in feature flag for customers.
Priya: i'll draft token v1 spec today. Noah will sketch transport adapter shapes and error types. Rae will add tests to the suite. Jordan will draft example code for docs.
build-bot: CI: pager-unify branch — tests passed (linux/py/ts) :white_check_mark:
Noah: one more: error model. Pager should expose PageError with properties {retryable: bool, cause}. don't hide transport-level Retry-After headers; surface them in error metadata.
Rae: and telemetry: emit events for resume_token_issued, token_version_mismatch, pager_retry, stream_to_pager_fallback. that'll help us observe production issues.
Jordan: cool. let's keep names stable and surface small, language-idiomatic primitives. follow-ups: priya token spec PR, noah transport sketch, rae tests. i'll start docs snippets.
Priya: posting token draft in #eng-platform when ready.
Noah: ping me for review.
Rae: will add flaky guard in CI for new tests.
Jordan: thanks all — keeping this minimal will make adoption easier. :thumbsup:
